question: The strongest initial share can fail confirmation while a smaller share helped on both training panels. Can the agent give that alternative one independent chance before keeping the incumbent?
status: Follow-up suggested by the two training panels, on reused stress development folds. The matched ordinary control scores were already known. The policy below is fixed before evaluating the follow-up; eligibility and shares depend exclusively on training feedback.
policy: Keep an already accepted population share. Otherwise require a nonzero share from the prior grid to be nonnegative on both existing inner profile-held panels, gain at least 0.20 percentage points pooled and have nonworsening pooled binary Brier. Rank eligible shares by higher worst-panel accuracy gain, then pooled accuracy gain, then lower pooled Brier change, then smaller share. Lock exactly one share before any new fit. If none is eligible, retain the incumbent with no new fit.
additional_evidence: Only on nomination, use group fold 1 under the same seed 39013; folds 0 and 3 supplied the old two scores. Refit the exact current incumbent, its actual seed members, and one population tree on the other four folds. Keep all held profiles outside both fits. Accept only if the third panel is nonnegative for accuracy and all three panels together still gain at least 0.20 percentage points with nonworsening Brier. On recognized profiles always keep the ordinary output. Count every additional classifier fit and reuse the sealed full-data population model. 64 units ceiling per treatment including its matched parent, both prior feedback panels and the extra panel.
advancement: Seal both folds' adaptive predictions before scoring. Require higher accuracy on both external stress folds and at least 0.30 percentage points net pooled before confirmation on previously unscored profile folds 1 and 2. No access to course validation or test.
